patch.value: A configured author_default suppresses harness detection entirely, so any workspace that sets a default author records no harness and no model provenance

resolveAuthorIdentity in src/core/shared/author.ts applies precedence explicit argument, then PM_AUTHOR, then configured author_default, then detected harness, then unknown — and returns EARLY at the configured branch. Detection therefore never runs in any workspace that sets author_default, and the harness field of the resolved identity is undefined even though the runtime signals were present and free to read. The same early return will suppress the model once model capture lands, so this defect silently cancels that capability for exactly the organizations most likely to configure defaults. The precedence order itself is correct and should not change: an operator who configures an author means it. What is wrong is treating detection as a fallback rather than as an always-available observation. Detection must run regardless of which branch supplied the author, with the detected harness, model, and session recorded as provenance beside the chosen author, and author_source continuing to report 'configured' so the asserted identity is never confused with the observed one.

Harness, model, and session detection runs on every mutation path regardless of which precedence branch supplied the author; The chosen author and its author_source discriminator are unchanged by this fix, proven by a test over all five precedence branches; A workspace with a configured author_default records the detected harness in its history entries while author_source remains 'configured'; An explicit --author or PM_AUTHOR override likewise records the observed provenance without changing the asserted author, so an override can never be used to erase which harness actually ran; The always-run detection call is asserted to stay within the mutation-path latency budget
Observed runtime provenance is recorded on every mutation regardless of which precedence branch supplied the author
Without this, the flagship fleet-attribution capability is unavailable precisely in configured, multi-agent, organizational workspaces — the deployments it exists to serve
Restores harness and model provenance for every workspace with a configured default author, at the cost of one always-run pure detection call on the mutation path
author_default keeps meaning what an operator configured it to mean, while the workspace still knows which harness and model actually ran
